title: Fork in the road

brief.story: Two status lights hang off the same 9 V column, each with its own resistor. The red one is bright, the green one barely glows. Someone sorted resistors by colour in bad light.
brief.goal: Light LED1 and LED2 at 10–25 mA each. Then the supply delivers both currents added together: between 30 and 50 mA.

hints: Measure across each resistor. Voltage ÷ resistance is the current through it, so you can compare the two branches without breaking the circuit.
R2 takes the same 6.8 V as R1 does, but its current is ten times smaller: its value is ten times too big. Orange-orange-red is 3.3 kΩ, not 330 Ω.
Click R2 and step its value down to 330 Ω.

spec.explain: The current splits at column 3 and joins again at the − rail, so the supply delivers the two branch currents added together.

debrief: The current splits where the two branches leave column 3 and joins again at the − rail. What flows into a point flows out of it (Kirchhoff's current law), so the supply delivers 21.2 mA + 20.6 mA = 41.8 mA. Each branch gets the full 9 V, which is why each LED needs its own resistor. And a colour code read in bad light is a factor of ten: orange-orange-brown is 330 Ω, orange-orange-red is 3.3 kΩ.
